clue.text: Painter departs, returning wise

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

indicators.note: returning means the word for wise is read backwards

parts.note: a sage person is a wise one

explanation.surface: A painter leaves, coming back wiser for the trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses only the word for wise; D is the timetable abbreviation, so it stays in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was the French Impressionist artist famous for his ballet dancers.

clue.text: Be contemptuous towards teacher — and send her packing

parts.note: to dis someone is to show them contempt, in slang
Miss is how pupils address a female teacher

explanation.surface: Someone scorns a teacher and then sacks her.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge someone from a job, or send them away, is to send them packing.

clue.text: Getting worse at skiing?

definitions.meaning: literally descending a slope, as a skier does

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means deteriorating; literally it describes heading down a slope, as skiers do.

clue.text: Buys Irishman a drink, and refuses any change

parts.note: to stand someone a drink is to buy one for them
Pat is a stock nickname for an Irishman, from Patrick

explanation.surface: A man treats his Irish friend to a drink but will not take his change.
explanation.walkthrough: STANDS here is the sense in 'stands a drink'; 'a drink' completes that surface reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from poker, means to stick firmly with one's position and resist alteration.

clue.text: English singer included in my official mission

indicators.note: included in means the singer is placed inside the word my

parts.note: a bass is a singer with the lowest voice

explanation.surface: An English vocalist has been added to my diplomatic delegation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' puts BASS between the M and Y of 'my', after E.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is a diplomatic mission sent officially by one state to another.

clue.text: Slavishly copies city gardens

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
to garden is to work the soil, as one hoes

explanation.surface: An urban planner imitates other cities' parks without thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gardens' is a verb here: hoes. EC is the City of London's postcode area.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat or imitate closely what others say or do is to reproduce them faithfully.

clue.text: British at work strike

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: British people at their jobs go on a walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit someone, especially with a light punch, is an informal way to strike them.

clue.text: Religious programme strangely forges passion

indicators.note: strangely means the letters of forges passion appear in an odd new arrangement

explanation.surface: A faith broadcast unexpectedly creates fervour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges FORGES PASSION; the programme is a long-running BBC hymn-singing show.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a long-running BBC Sunday television show of hymn singing and worship.

clue.text: Finally buy beer in university

indicators.note: Finally picks out the last letter of the word buy

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: At last a student buys a beer on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an Ivy League institution of higher learning in New Haven, Connecticut.

clue.text: With end of fingers, squeeze round a vegetable

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word fingers
round means the squeezing word goes around the letter a

parts.note: to pinch is to squeeze between finger and thumb

explanation.surface: Using your fingertips, squeeze a vegetable such as a tomato to test it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' places A inside PINCH, giving PINACH, after the S that ends 'fingers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green plant eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Section of door and piece of window left

parts.note: a pane is a single sheet of glass in a window

explanation.surface: A joiner describes parts of a door and a broken bit of window to his left.
explanation.definitionFit: Doors are often built from framed flat sections, each called by this carpentry term.

clue.text: Doing badly, is our hope: some national motto!

indicators.note: badly means the letters of the word doing are jumbled

parts.note: to say we trust is to say something is our hope or belief

explanation.surface: A national team is doing badly, and a slogan is all the hope left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges DOING into INGOD; the phrase 'is our hope' is rendered as WE TRUST.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is the official motto of the United States, printed on its banknotes and coins.

clue.text: Purchasing power of earnings law agrees must be adjusted

indicators.note: must be adjusted means the letters of law agrees are reordered

explanation.surface: Legislation concedes that pay must be revised for its buying power.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists use the term for pay after allowing for inflation, which is what it can actually buy.

clue.text: Cartoon dog tending to pry?

definitions.meaning: the beagle in Charles Schulz's Peanuts comic strip
inclined to poke into other people's business, nosy

explanation.surface: A comic-strip pet with an inquisitive nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Brown's beagle in Peanuts carries this name; as an adjective it means nosy or inquisitive.

clue.text: Boss is right to go after mistake

indicators.note: to go after means this letter is placed following the mistake

parts.note: a gaffe is an embarrassing mistake

explanation.surface: The boss is right to come after you when you have blundered.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal speech a foreman or employer is called by this word.

clue.text: Considerately treat relation

definitions.meaning: to regard someone or something with esteem and care
a connection or particular point, as in 'with regard to'

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to honour; as a noun, a particular aspect or point of reference.

clue.text: One in the club, married, remains smouldering

parts.note: an ember is a piece of a fire still glowing among the ashes

explanation.surface: A married clubman's passion still smoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who belongs to a club or society is one of its enrolled people.

clue.text: To be clear, moved with no orders

indicators.note: moved means the letters of with no orders are shifted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: To put it plainly, someone has left without being ordered to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges the twelve letters of WITH NO ORDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a restatement in simpler terms, so it serves to make a point clearer.

clue.text: Cornish sailor's mop?

parts.note: Cornwall is in the south-west of England, abbreviated SW
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor from Cornwall cleans the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is England's south-western county, hence SW.
explanation.definitionFit: A mop for cleaning decks on a ship, or a pad for wiping, goes by this name.

clue.text: Measure the announced route

indicators.note: announced means the word for route is spoken, and the matching sound spelt otherwise

parts.note: a way is a route or road

explanation.surface: A guide gauges the route that has just been declared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' signals the sound of WAY, spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To find how heavy something is on scales is to measure it in that way.

clue.text: Almost loathe bowler, for one

indicators.note: Almost means the last letter of the word for loathe is dropped

parts.note: to hate is to loathe

explanation.surface: A batsman nearly detests a particular bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' wants to be a cricketer; it is the round-crowned hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler is a hard felt hat with a rounded crown, so it is one example of headwear.

clue.text: Long period at the top of eg show business

definitions.text: the top of eg show business

parts.note: big can mean large or long, as in a big gap
a time is a period, as in a time of plenty

explanation.surface: A star has had a lengthy spell at the summit of the entertainment world.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching this level means attaining the highest, most successful rank in a field such as entertainment.

clue.text: One running away receives small support

indicators.note: receives means the runaway takes the letter for small inside it

parts.note: a bolter is a horse or person that runs off

explanation.surface: A fugitive is given a little help.
explanation.definitionFit: To shore up or prop something is to give it support, as a long pillow does.

clue.text: In short autumn month wife did some cleaning

indicators.note: In means the letter for wife goes inside the shortened month

parts.note: Sept is the short form of September

explanation.surface: A wife did a little housework in a brief autumn month.
explanation.definitionFit: Using a brush or broom on a floor is a common way of cleaning it.
